Whittaker fits generalized additive models in Python: regressions in which each effect is a smooth
curve learned from the data, with **its smoothness chosen automatically**. It brings the depth of
R's mgcv to Pandas, Polars, and any [Narwhals](https://narwhals-dev.github.io/narwhals/)
DataFrame, with an interactive chart for every fit.

## A model, one term at a time {.wkh-heading}

A GAM is a formula of smooth terms, fitted in one call. Step through this one, on four decades of
CO₂ readings from Mauna Loa, to see what each term adds, with the new lines of code highlighted.

::::: {.wkh-stepper #wkh-stepper}

:::: {.wkh-step}
[Data]{.wkh-step-name}

Start with a data frame. This one, one of Whittaker's built-in datasets, has a reading for every
month from 1958 to 1997: a rising trend with a yearly cycle on top.

```{python}
import altair as alt
import whittaker as wk

co2 = wk.load_dataset("co2", as_frame=True)

chart = alt.Chart(co2).encode(x=alt.X("t:Q", title=None, axis=alt.Axis(format="d")))
data = chart.mark_line(color="#c4bccb").encode(
    y=alt.Y("co2:Q", title="CO₂ (ppm)", scale=alt.Scale(zero=False))
)

data.properties(width="container", height=280)
```
::::

:::: {.wkh-step}
[Trend]{.wkh-step-name}

`s(t)` is a smooth function of time, with no shape assumed. Its wiggliness is penalized, and the
penalty's weight is chosen from the data, so the curve follows the trend and not the noise.

```{python}
import altair as alt
import whittaker as wk

co2 = wk.load_dataset("co2", as_frame=True)

model = wk.GAM("co2 ~ s(t)").fit(co2)
co2["fit"] = model.predict(co2).values

chart = alt.Chart(co2).encode(x=alt.X("t:Q", title=None, axis=alt.Axis(format="d")))
data = chart.mark_line(color="#c4bccb").encode(
    y=alt.Y("co2:Q", title="CO₂ (ppm)", scale=alt.Scale(zero=False))
)
fit = chart.mark_line(color="#b8405f", strokeWidth=1.5).encode(y="fit:Q")

(data + fit).properties(width="container", height=280)
```
::::

:::: {.wkh-step}
[Season]{.wkh-step-name}

Add a second smooth, of the month. A cyclic basis (`bs="cc"`) makes December meet January, and the
two terms are fitted together: now the curve tracks every season.

```{python}
import altair as alt
import whittaker as wk

co2 = wk.load_dataset("co2", as_frame=True)

model = wk.GAM("co2 ~ s(t) + s(month, bs='cc', k=12)").fit(co2)
co2["fit"] = model.predict(co2).values

chart = alt.Chart(co2).encode(x=alt.X("t:Q", title=None, axis=alt.Axis(format="d")))
data = chart.mark_line(color="#c4bccb").encode(
    y=alt.Y("co2:Q", title="CO₂ (ppm)", scale=alt.Scale(zero=False))
)
fit = chart.mark_line(color="#b8405f", strokeWidth=1.5).encode(y="fit:Q")

(data + fit).properties(width="container", height=280)
```
::::

:::: {.wkh-step}
[Effects]{.wkh-step-name}

Each term can be seen on its own. [`model.plot()`](reference/GAM.qmd) draws every smooth's
partial effect, with its confidence band and its effective degrees of freedom.

```{python}
import whittaker as wk

co2 = wk.load_dataset("co2", as_frame=True)

model = wk.GAM("co2 ~ s(t) + s(month, bs='cc', k=12)").fit(co2)

model.plot()
```
::::

:::: {.wkh-step}
[Summary]{.wkh-step-name}

[`model.summary()`](reference/GAM.qmd) gives the model's numbers: each smooth's effective degrees of
freedom and significance test, the deviance explained, and the AIC.

```{python}
import whittaker as wk

co2 = wk.load_dataset("co2", as_frame=True)

model = wk.GAM("co2 ~ s(t) + s(month, bs='cc', k=12)").fit(co2)

model.summary()
```
::::

:::: {.wkh-step}
[Check]{.wkh-step-name}

[`wk.check()`](reference/check.qmd) asks whether the model can be trusted: the residuals against
the fit, their quantiles and histogram, and the observed values against the fitted ones.

```{python}
import whittaker as wk

co2 = wk.load_dataset("co2", as_frame=True)

model = wk.GAM("co2 ~ s(t) + s(month, bs='cc', k=12)").fit(co2)

wk.check(model)
```
::::

## Every kind of smooth {.wkh-heading}

Thin plate and cubic splines, P-splines, cyclic and adaptive smooths, Gaussian processes, random
effects, tensor products for surfaces, and smooths held to a shape (increasing, decreasing, convex,
or concave). Each tile here is a real fit, so select one to read about it.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import numpy as np
from IPython.display import HTML

_W, _H, _PAD = 230, 112, 8
_rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
_x = np.sort(_rng.uniform(0, 1, 120))
_noise = _rng.normal(0, 1, 120)
_grid = np.linspace(0, 1, 90)
_shapes = {
    "wave": lambda x: np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + 0.5 * np.sin(5 * np.pi * x),
    "cycle": lambda x: np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + 0.4 * np.cos(4 * np.pi * x),
    "doppler": lambda x: np.sin(1.5 / (x + 0.12)) * np.sqrt(x + 0.05),
    "rise": lambda x: 2 / (1 + np.exp(-12 * (x - 0.5))),
    "fall": lambda x: -2 / (1 + np.exp(-12 * (x - 0.5))),
    "convex": lambda x: 3 * (x - 0.4) ** 2,
    "concave": lambda x: -3 * (x - 0.6) ** 2,
}


def _scale(values, lo, hi, a, b):
    return a + (np.asarray(values) - lo) / (hi - lo) * (b - a)


def _svg(body):
    return f'<svg viewBox="0 0 {_W} {_H}" role="img" aria-hidden="true">{body}</svg>'


# A smooth of one variable: the data, the fit, and its band (two standard errors either side)
def _curve_tile(bs, shape, k=""):
    y = _shapes[shape](_x) + 0.25 * _noise
    fitted = wk.GAM(f"y ~ s(x, bs='{bs}'{k})").fit({"x": _x, "y": y}, method="REML")
    pred = fitted.predict({"x": _grid}, se=True)
    fit, se = np.asarray(pred.values), np.asarray(pred.se)
    lo, hi = min(y.min(), (fit - 2 * se).min()), max(y.max(), (fit + 2 * se).max())
    sx = lambda v: _scale(v, 0, 1, _PAD, _W - _PAD)
    sy = lambda v: _scale(v, lo, hi, _H - _PAD, _PAD)
    gx = sx(_grid)
    upper = " ".join(f"{a:.1f},{b:.1f}" for a, b in zip(gx, sy(fit + 2 * se)))
    lower = " ".join(f"{a:.1f},{b:.1f}" for a, b in zip(gx[::-1], sy((fit - 2 * se)[::-1])))
    points = "".join(f'<circle cx="{a:.1f}" cy="{b:.1f}" r="1.8"/>' for a, b in zip(sx(_x), sy(y)))
    curve = " ".join(f"{a:.1f},{b:.1f}" for a, b in zip(gx, sy(fit)))
    return _svg(
        f'<polygon class="wkh-band" points="{upper} {lower}"/>'
        f'<g class="wkh-pts">{points}</g>'
        f'<polyline class="wkh-curve" points="{curve}"/>'
    )


# A smooth of two variables: the fitted surface, as a grid of cells
def _surface_tile(term):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
    x1, x2 = rng.uniform(0, 1, 400), rng.uniform(0, 1, 400)
    y = np.sin(2.4 * np.pi * x1) * np.cos(1.6 * np.pi * x2) + 0.6 * (x1 - x2)
    y = y + rng.normal(0, 0.2, 400)
    fitted = wk.GAM(f"y ~ {term}").fit({"x1": x1, "x2": x2, "y": y}, method="REML")
    nx, ny = 26, 13
    g1, g2 = np.meshgrid((np.arange(nx) + 0.5) / nx, (np.arange(ny) + 0.5) / ny)
    fit = np.asarray(fitted.predict({"x1": g1.ravel(), "x2": g2.ravel()}).values)
    top = np.abs(fit).max()
    cw, ch = _W / nx, _H / ny
    cells = "".join(
        f'<rect class="{"wkh-pos" if v > 0 else "wkh-neg"}" x="{a * _W - cw / 2:.1f}" '
        f'y="{_H - b * _H - ch / 2:.1f}" width="{cw + 0.3:.1f}" height="{ch + 0.3:.1f}" '
        f'fill-opacity="{abs(v) / top:.2f}"/>'
        for a, b, v in zip(g1.ravel(), g2.ravel(), fit)
    )
    return _svg(cells)


# A factor smooth: a curve for each of four groups
def _factor_tile():
    xx = np.tile(np.linspace(0, 1, 30), 4)
    g = np.repeat(np.array(["a", "b", "c", "d"]), 30)
    y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * xx + np.repeat([0.0, 0.8, 1.6, 2.4], 30)) + _rng.normal(0, 0.2, 120)
    fitted = wk.GAM("y ~ s(x, g, bs='fs')").fit({"x": xx, "g": g, "y": y})
    sx = lambda v: _scale(v, 0, 1, _PAD, _W - _PAD)
    sy = lambda v: _scale(v, -1.8, 1.8, _H - _PAD, _PAD)
    body = ""
    for k, level in enumerate("abcd"):
        fit = np.asarray(fitted.predict({"x": _grid, "g": np.full(_grid.size, level)}).values)
        line = " ".join(f"{a:.1f},{b:.1f}" for a, b in zip(sx(_grid), sy(fit)))
        body += f'<polyline class="wkh-curve" style="opacity:{1 - 0.2 * k}" points="{line}"/>'
    return _svg(body)


# A random effect: each group's observations, and its estimate (shrunk toward the overall mean)
def _random_tile():
    levels = np.array(list("abcdefghij"))
    g = np.repeat(levels, 6)
    y = np.repeat(np.random.default_rng(5).normal(0, 1, 10), 6)
    y = y + np.random.default_rng(6).normal(0, 0.8, 60)
    fitted = wk.GAM("y ~ s(g, bs='re')").fit({"g": g, "y": y}, method="REML")
    fit = np.asarray(fitted.predict({"g": levels}).values)
    lo, hi = y.min() - 0.2, y.max() + 0.2
    sx = lambda i: _PAD + 12 + i * (_W - 2 * _PAD - 24) / 9
    sy = lambda v: _scale(v, lo, hi, _H - _PAD, _PAD)
    points = "".join(
        f'<circle cx="{sx(i // 6) + (i % 6 - 2.5) * 1.6:.1f}" cy="{sy(v):.1f}" r="1.8"/>'
        for i, v in enumerate(y)
    )
    bars = "".join(
        f'<line class="wkh-curve" x1="{sx(i) - 8:.1f}" x2="{sx(i) + 8:.1f}" '
        f'y1="{sy(v):.1f}" y2="{sy(v):.1f}"/>'
        for i, v in enumerate(fit)
    )
    return _svg(f'<g class="wkh-pts">{points}</g>{bars}')


# The tiles (each: its page in the User Guide, its term, its name, and how it's drawn), in two rows
_rows = [
    [
        ("smooths.html#tprs", "s(x)", "Thin plate", lambda: _curve_tile("tp", "wave")),
        ("smooths.html#crs", 's(x, bs="cr")', "Cubic", lambda: _curve_tile("cr", "wave")),
        ("smooths.html#psplines", 's(x, bs="ps")', "P-spline", lambda: _curve_tile("ps", "wave")),
        ("smooths.html#cyclic", 's(x, bs="cc")', "Cyclic", lambda: _curve_tile("cc", "cycle")),
        ("smooths.html#shrinkage", 's(x, bs="ts")', "Shrinkage", lambda: _curve_tile("ts", "wave")),
        (
            "smooths.html#adaptive",
            's(x, bs="ad")',
            "Adaptive",
            lambda: _curve_tile("ad", "doppler", ", k=40"),
        ),
        ("smooths.html#gp", 's(x, bs="gp")', "Gaussian process", lambda: _curve_tile("gp", "wave")),
        ("smooths.html#random-effects", 's(g, bs="re")', "Random effect", _random_tile),
        ("smooths.html#fs", 's(x, g, bs="fs")', "Factor smooth", _factor_tile),
    ],
    [
        ("smooths.html#tensor", "te(x1, x2)", "Tensor product", lambda: _surface_tile("te(x1, x2)")),
        (
            "shape-constraints.html#monotone-increasing",
            's(x, bs="mpi")',
            "Increasing",
            lambda: _curve_tile("mpi", "rise"),
        ),
        (
            "shape-constraints.html#monotone-decreasing",
            's(x, bs="mpd")',
            "Decreasing",
            lambda: _curve_tile("mpd", "fall"),
        ),
        ("smooths.html#tprs", "s(x1, x2)", "Thin plate, 2-D", lambda: _surface_tile("s(x1, x2)")),
        ("shape-constraints.html#convex", 's(x, bs="cx")', "Convex", lambda: _curve_tile("cx", "convex")),
        (
            "shape-constraints.html#concave",
            's(x, bs="cv")',
            "Concave",
            lambda: _curve_tile("cv", "concave"),
        ),
        ("smooths.html#tensor", "t2(x1, x2)", "Tensor (t2)", lambda: _surface_tile("t2(x1, x2)")),
        ("smooths.html#cyclic", 's(x, bs="cp")', "Cyclic P-spline", lambda: _curve_tile("cp", "cycle")),
        ("smooths.html", 's(x1, x2, bs="ds")', "Duchon", lambda: _surface_tile("s(x1, x2, bs='ds')")),
    ],
]


def _tile(page, term, name, draw):
    return (
        f'<a class="wkh-tile" href="user-guide/{page}">{draw()}'
        f'<span class="wkh-tile-name"><code>{term}</code><span>{name}</span></span></a>'
    )


HTML(
    '<div class="wkh-marquee" role="region" aria-label="Smooths from the User Guide">'
    + "".join(
        f'<div class="wkh-marquee-row{" wkh-reverse" if k else ""}">'
        f'<div class="wkh-marquee-track">{"".join(_tile(*spec) for spec in row)}</div></div>'
        for k, row in enumerate(_rows)
    )
    + "</div>"
)
```

## Four ways to draw a band {.wkh-heading}

The head's acceleration in a simulated motorcycle crash spreads out after the impact. Each of these
models puts a 90% band around it in its own way.

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "How the charts are drawn"
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

mcycle = wk.load_dataset("mcycle", as_frame=True)
grid = pd.DataFrame({"times": np.linspace(0, 57, 200)})


# The data, and a curve with a band around it
def show(middle, lower, upper):
    band = grid.assign(middle=middle, lower=lower, upper=upper)
    x = alt.X("times:Q", title="Time after impact (ms)")
    return (
        alt.Chart(band).mark_area(color="#d36983", opacity=0.18).encode(x=x, y="lower:Q", y2="upper:Q")
        + alt.Chart(mcycle).mark_circle(color="#9a8aa8", size=22).encode(
            x=x, y=alt.Y("accel:Q", title="Acceleration (g)")
        )
        + alt.Chart(band).mark_line(color="#b8405f", strokeWidth=2).encode(x=x, y="middle:Q")
    ).properties(width="container", height=300)
```

::::: {.wkh-switch #wkh-switch}

:::: {.wkh-option}
[Mean]{.wkh-option-name}

A GAM's prediction interval has one width everywhere, so it is too wide before the impact and too
narrow after it.

```{python}
model = wk.GAM("accel ~ s(times, k=20)").fit(mcycle, method="REML")
pred = model.predict(grid, interval="prediction", level=0.9)

show(pred.values, pred.lower, pred.upper)
```
::::

:::: {.wkh-option}
[Location and scale]{.wkh-option-name}

A GAMLSS model gives the spread its own smooth, alongside the mean's, and the band follows the
spread as it changes.

```{python}
model = wk.GAMLSS(
    formulas={"mu": "accel ~ s(times, k=20)", "sigma": "accel ~ s(times)"},
    family=wk.GaussianLS(),
).fit(mcycle)
pred = model.predict(grid).values

show(pred["mu"], pred["mu"] - 1.645 * pred["sigma"], pred["mu"] + 1.645 * pred["sigma"])
```
::::

:::: {.wkh-option}
[Quantiles]{.wkh-option-name}

Quantile regression fits the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles directly, with no distribution assumed
for the noise.

```{python}
model = wk.QuantileGAM("accel ~ s(times, k=15)", quantiles=[0.05, 0.5, 0.95]).fit(mcycle)
pred = model.predict(grid)

show(pred[0.5].values, pred[0.05].values, pred[0.95].values)
```
::::

:::: {.wkh-option}
[Conformal]{.wkh-option-name}

Conformal prediction wraps any model in an interval with guaranteed coverage, from the model's
errors on data it wasn't fitted to.

```{python}
model = wk.conformal_fit("accel ~ s(times, k=20)", mcycle, method="cv+", level=0.9, seed=1)
pred = model.predict(grid)

show(pred.values, pred.lower, pred.upper)
```
::::

## And when you need more {.wkh-heading}

:::: {.wkh-cards}

::: {.wkh-card}
[<i class="bi bi-diagram-3"></i>]{.wkh-card-icon}

#### Families for any response

Counts, proportions, positive and skewed values, survival times, ordered and unordered categories,
and zero-inflated data, each with its own links.

[Response families →](user-guide/families.qmd)
:::

::: {.wkh-card}
[<i class="bi bi-shuffle"></i>]{.wkh-card-icon}

#### Bayesian inference

Variational inference for a fast posterior, or NUTS sampling with R-hat, effective sample sizes,
and divergences, then LOO, WAIC, and stacking.

[MCMC sampling →](user-guide/mcmc.qmd)
:::

::: {.wkh-card}
[<i class="bi bi-database"></i>]{.wkh-card-icon}

#### Large datasets

`BigGAM` fits millions of rows by discretizing them, and `PolarsGAM` and `DuckDBGAM` stream data
that doesn't fit in memory.

[Large datasets →](user-guide/large-datasets.qmd)
:::

::: {.wkh-card}
[<i class="bi bi-bezier2"></i>]{.wkh-card-icon}

#### Causal inference

Average and conditional treatment effects by double machine learning, with smooths for the
nuisance models, and mediation analysis.

[Causal inference →](user-guide/causal.qmd)
:::

::: {.wkh-card}
[<i class="bi bi-activity"></i>]{.wkh-card-icon}

#### Streaming and functional data

Update a model as data arrives, tracking drift with decay, or regress a scalar on a whole curve.

[Streaming and online fitting →](user-guide/streaming.qmd)
:::

::: {.wkh-card}
[<i class="bi bi-graph-up-arrow"></i>]{.wkh-card-icon}

#### Derivatives and comparisons

Derivatives and marginal effects with simultaneous bands, ANOVA, and side-by-side comparisons of
models.

[Derivatives and marginal effects →](user-guide/derivatives.qmd)
:::

::: {.wkh-card}
[<i class="bi bi-puzzle"></i>]{.wkh-card-icon}

#### scikit-learn

`GAMRegressor` and `GAMClassifier` go into pipelines, grid searches, and cross-validation like any
other estimator.

[scikit-learn integration →](user-guide/sklearn.qmd)
:::

::: {.wkh-card}
[<i class="bi bi-save"></i>]{.wkh-card-icon}

#### Save, load, and share with R

Save a fitted model to a compact file, and convert it to and from mgcv's form for R.

[Saving and loading models →](user-guide/serialization.qmd)
:::

::: {.wkh-card}
[<i class="bi bi-code-slash"></i>]{.wkh-card-icon}

#### Formulas in code

Build models from terms in code as well as from formula strings, and get their model matrices for
your own work.

[Programmatic formulas →](user-guide/programmatic-formulas.qmd)
:::

## Get started {.wkh-heading}

:::: {.wkh-start}

::: {.wkh-start-text}

```bash
pip install whittaker
```

Then fit your first models in the [Quick start](user-guide/quick-start.qmd), learn how GAMs work in
[Understanding GAMs](user-guide/understanding-gams.qmd), or find a recipe for a task in the
[Cookbook](cookbook/fit-your-first-smooth.qmd).
